text: To the woman at the well, Jesus promised a well. At the feast, He promised rivers. A well is for you; rivers are for everyone around you.
explanation:
In John 4 the drinking is a one-time act: drink once, and a well springs up inside you to everlasting life. That's the new birth. In John 7, on the last great day of the feast, Jesus cried, "If anyone thirsts, let him come to Me and drink," and the Greek is continuous: keep coming, keep drinking. Then "out of his heart will flow rivers of living water." John explains that He spoke of the Spirit.

In Jesus' day, a man could own a well, but rivers belonged to everyone. You can be saved and still be no blessing to anyone around you. When the rivers flow, "everything will live wherever the river goes," as Ezekiel saw the river from the temple bring even the Dead Sea to life.

text: At Pentecost there was wind and fire. In the rest of Acts, those receiving the Spirit didn't always see wind or fire, but they always spoke.
explanation:
The common denominator when people were filled with the Spirit in Acts was speaking: in tongues, or prophesying. "They began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance." They spoke; the Spirit gave the words. God won't force your mouth open. Evil spirits drive; the Holy Spirit leads. When the strange words come, speak them out.

Paul says, "Be filled with the Spirit, speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs." Then he goes straight on to husbands, wives, children and work. A Spirit-filled life is the oil in the machinery of marriage. Pray in the Spirit, and you'll find you're keeping yourself in the love of God.

text: "He who speaks in a tongue edifies himself": he charges himself up like a battery. And how much you charge is up to you.
explanation:
Nobody shows off their phone while it charges. It happens quietly, usually at night. Praying in tongues is like that: unglamorous, but you come out charged and ready to meet whatever negative situation you find. Some think they can only pray in tongues when the music is playing and the Spirit is moving. But Paul said, "I will pray with the spirit." It's a choice, any time, as long as you like.

Why is it so powerful? The temple had an outer court, a holy place and a most holy place. You're body, soul and spirit. Praying with your understanding is praying from the holy place. "If I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays," from the most holy place where God dwells. That's how you build yourself up "on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit."

text: "The Spirit also helps in our weaknesses." The Greek pictures Him taking hold together with you, against the problem.
explanation:
"We do not know what we should pray for as we ought." Paul included himself. Your baby won't stop crying and the doctor says it's normal. You don't know exactly what's wrong. But the Spirit does, and He "makes intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered": not in any language you know.

The word for "helps" is sunantilambanetai: sun (together with), anti (against), lambanō (take hold). He doesn't do it all while you do nothing. When you take hold of the problem by praying in the Spirit, He takes hold with you, and together you shift it. When you let go, He lets go. Pray until there's a release, a quiet peace that you've prayed through.

text: On the highway, he felt a sense of danger and prayed in the Spirit until peace came. Minutes later, a truck crossed into his lane.
explanation:
A minister was driving with his wife asleep beside him when an unease came over him. He prayed quietly in tongues, eyes open, until he sensed a release. Soon after, a truck lost control and came into his lane. He swerved, and it smashed into the small car behind him, crushing the driver's side. When he ran back, he found the driver unhurt, sitting in the passenger seat with no idea how he got there. The Spirit whispered, "This is what you were praying for."

You don't have to be on your knees, and you don't have to understand every word. If you knew everything the Spirit was praying, you might lock your children indoors for five years! Just pray, while cooking, driving, or sitting in a meeting, until peace comes.

text: "With stammering lips and another tongue He will speak to this people… This is the rest… and this is the refreshing." Yet they would not hear.
explanation:
Paul quotes Isaiah when he writes about tongues. Centuries earlier, God foresaw a gift for His people: rest for the weary and refreshing for the soul. He also foresaw that many would refuse it. You can often gauge how powerful a truth is by how fiercely it's opposed, and churches have split over this simple gift.

"Let us be diligent to enter that rest." At first, praying in tongues can feel like labour. Keep going. Inner fears, knots of anxiety and panic, things even your spouse doesn't know about, are like logs and rubbish clogging a river. The longer it flows, the more it clears, until it runs free. A running river is clean, refreshing, and it generates power.

text: God designed your spirit to lead, your soul to follow, and your body to serve. That's what it means to be truly together.
explanation:
When Adam sinned, his spirit died: cut off from God. Since then, people tend to live either from the mind, so clever they reason God out of everything, or from the body, driven by appetite. When you're born again, your spirit comes alive, but it starts as a baby while your mind has been in charge for years. When you pray in tongues, your mind says, "This is nonsense. Stop!"

Keep praying. Eventually the mind surrenders, not destroyed but enhanced, becoming the servant it was meant to be. Experienced fishermen who'd caught nothing all night had every reason to argue with a carpenter. When they let down the nets at His word, the nets broke with fish. Let your spirit lead.
